# phase-041 — Implement `text.split` and `text.join`, and pin which stdlib names are reachable dotted

## You must change `src/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [src/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
SPEC.md's Standard Library section documents `set parts to text.split("a,b,c", by ",")` and `set joined to text.join(["a", "b", "c"], by ",")`. src/runtime.rs:263 (`pub fn builtin`) matches 30 names and NEITHER `split` NOR `join` is among them; there is no `text` module object either, so the two functions do not exist in any spelling. Verified against the built binary: `set p to text.split("a,b", by ",")` exits 1 with `AnalyzerError: Unknown variable 'text'`. The same probe shows the dotted form is not uniformly absent, which is why the gap is invisible: `files.read("examples/hello.rb")` DOES resolve — src/interpreter.rs:914 `call_method` maps a receiver naming no object onto the flat `files_read` builtin, as its own doc comment says — and the flat `uppercase`/`lowercase` exist at src/stdlib.rs:220 and :227. So a program written from SPEC.md fails on `text.split` while succeeding on `files.read`, and no document says which is which. `split` and `join` are also two of the four primitives a lexer needs to read its own source.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Implement `text.split` and `text.join` as real builtins, and make the dotted-versus-flat call form a documented property of the stdlib rather than an accident.

## Definition of done

- [ ] table-driven tests pin the answer for each of: an empty subject, a subject equal to the separator, a separator absent from the subject, adjacent separators, and a 3-character separator — including what `text.split("", by ",")` returns and what `text.join([], by ",")` returns
- [ ] each of those cases prints byte-identical output under `rb run` and under `rb vm` on the output of `rb compile`
- [ ] `split` and `join` given a non-list or non-text argument produce a CAUGHT RuntimeError naming the builtin, not a panic
- [ ] REPORT.md contains one table naming, for every builtin in src/runtime.rs and src/stdlib.rs, whether it is reachable dotted and whether it is reachable flat, with the line that decides it — and either the dotted form works for all of them or SPEC.md is amended to say exactly which are flat-only
- [ ] edge_* tests cover the empty subject, the empty list, an empty separator, and a subject longer than the separator
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets` reports 0 failures, including the 39 tests in tests/stdlib_modules_test.rs and the 8 files in examples/ and modules/ all exiting 0
